study type: Prospective, confirmatory, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (Randomized Controlled Trial)
exposure: Oral administration of Escherichia coli Nissle 1917
cohort: The study enrolled 567 healthy neonates from Germany and Poland.
finding: Oral administration of E. coli Nissle 1917 did not show a statistically significant long-term effect in reducing the number, duration, or severity of infections after 24 months, though a short-term benefit was observed up to eight weeks.
gest_age: Term neonates (implied by title and 'healthy neonates')
